evals.name: default-style-from-outline
evals.prompt: Build me a 6-slide HTML presentation introducing our team's new code-review automation policy to engineering. Slides: (1) title, (2) why the policy exists — three reasons, (3) what changes in PR flow, (4) tooling we'll roll out — three tools in a card row, (5) what we're measuring — three KPI callouts, (6) timeline and Q&A. Save it to ./code-review-policy.html. Don't ask me which style — pick a sensible default.
evals.expected_output: 6-slide HTML deck at ./code-review-policy.html using style-1 (Executive Steel), varied layouts, theme CSS inlined, Google Fonts link present, Reveal.js CDN loaded, no reference to ./style.md.

assertions.text: code-review-policy.html exists and is a valid HTML file
Document contains exactly 6 <section class="layout-*"> elements
Slide content covers all 6 outline sections (policy/reasons, PR flow, tooling, KPIs/metrics, timeline)
At least 3 distinct layout archetypes used across the deck (e.g. title, card-row, bigNumber)
No leftover placeholder text (lorem, xxxx, TODO, 'Deck title goes here')
A style was chosen and applied — consistent palette via CSS variables across slides
<style> block present and scoped under .reveal
Google Fonts <link> with display=swap present
Reveal.js CDN <script> tag present, pinned to a specific version (not @latest)
Output HTML does NOT reference ./style.md (grep for 'style.md' returns 0 matches)

evals.name: named-style-editorial-light
evals.prompt: Use the editorial-light style to create an 8-slide HTML pitch deck for a hypothetical research product called 'Hindsight' — an AI-powered post-mortem tool for engineering teams. Outline: title, problem (no visibility into past incidents), solution overview, three product capabilities (in a card row), demo screenshot placeholder, customer logos placeholder, pricing tiers (in a card row with 3 tiers), closing CTA. Output to ./hindsight-pitch.html. After building, run polish-deck.py and report what it flagged.
evals.expected_output: 8-slide HTML deck at ./hindsight-pitch.html using editorial-light palette, two card-row slides, polish-deck.py output captured.

assertions.text: hindsight-pitch.html exists and is a valid HTML file
Document contains exactly 8 <section class="layout-*"> elements
CSS variable --color-bg has the editorial-light style's bg hex value
CSS variable --color-accent has the editorial-light style's accent hex value
At least one slide uses layout-card-row with 2-4 cards
polish-deck.py was run against the output and its result is reported
Title slide mentions 'Hindsight' product name
No leftover placeholder text
Output HTML does NOT reference ./style.md or any external .css file (only Reveal CDN + Google Fonts allowed)

evals.name: style-mimicry-from-website
evals.prompt: I like the visual style of https://stripe.com — derive a brandbook from it and use it to build me a 5-slide HTML deck on 'Observability for Agent Systems'. Save to ./observability-deck.html. Tell me about any heuristics the derivation may have gotten wrong.
evals.expected_output: 5-slide HTML deck at ./observability-deck.html, brandbook derived from stripe.com via load-style.js (or equivalent), notes documenting derivation caveats.

assertions.text: observability-deck.html exists and is a valid HTML file
Document contains exactly 5 <section class="layout-*"> elements
Slide text covers observability topic (mentions observability/agents/monitoring/traces)
A derived style.md was created (either via load-style.js or hand-authored from inspected CSS)
Derivation caveats are documented in a notes.md or in chat (palette/font heuristics may be off)
Layouts are varied — at least 3 distinct layout archetypes
Output HTML does NOT reference ./style.md
